title: Zero Support
body: I genuinely loved this game. I loved the community, building teams, talking to people, and especially the union system. Being part of a 100-player union where everyone works together, builds the group from the ground up, and creates its own culture was easily the best part of the game. I met a lot of genuinely great people through this game and had an amazing time playing with them. What I didn’t love was how important spending money is if you actually want to stay competitive. I normally don’t spend money on games, but I ended up spending well over $100 on this one. I wasn’t randomly buying things either; I was buying things I felt I needed just to have a reasonable chance of staying relevant. The packs can look like good value individually, but they add up extremely quickly. And when you have players spending hundreds or even thousands of dollars, the whole system becomes pretty ridiculous. But the money isn’t even the biggest problem. After spending months building my account, developing my teams, and becoming part of this community, my account was suddenly blocked for an “improper refund.” The problem is that I have never requested a refund. Not once. I regret some of the money I spent, sure, but I never requested a refund through the game. So I tried to contact support. I followed the account-block instructions and was directed to their official Facebook page. I downloaded Messenger so I could contact them there, only to find that I was talking to a bot. The bot repeatedly told me to access the manual customer service option inside the game. I kept explaining that I cannot access the game because MY ACCOUNT IS BLOCKED, so I cannot access the customer service option inside the game. It just kept giving me the same response. I then contacted two different email addresses that were supposedly official support addresses. I sent those emails over two weeks ago and have received absolutely no response. I’ve even had friends try contacting support on my behalf, and that hasn’t worked either. I also tried uninstalling and reinstalling the game because I thought maybe I could simply create a new account and start over. That didn’t work either. Even after reinstalling, I’m still blocked and can’t get into the game. At this point, I’ve spent months of my time and well over $100 on a game that I genuinely loved, only to suddenly lose access to everything without even being told what I supposedly did wrong. The money is frustrating, but honestly, the time and the community hurt much more. I had over 100 people in this community who I genuinely considered friends. These were people I talked to every day, played with, and built something with. Now I’m essentially cut off from all of that because I can’t access the game, and I still don’t even know why my account was blocked in the first place. This situation caused me a lot of stress for weeks while I tried to get it resolved. At this point, I’ve basically accepted that I may never be able to play again, despite never requesting the refund that supposedly caused my account to be blocked. My advice to new players: enjoy the game and enjoy the community, but be extremely careful about how much time and money you invest. You can spend months building an account and making friends, only to have your access taken away, with no effective way to reach a real person and no clear explanation of what happened. I really did love this game. That’s what makes this situation so disappointing.

title: Bait and switch- becomes zombie game.

Two minutes in, the dog vanishes and I'm suddenly commanding an army against waves of zombies with guns, gore, and a cash shop begging me to buy grenades. No bees. No dog. No barrier-building. Just another generic tower-defense/shooter clone wearing a stolen mascot as a mask. This bait-and-switch advertising is so common on the app store it's almost a genre of its own at this point, but that doesn't make it okay. If I wanted a zombie shooter I'd have searched for one. title: Addictive
body: Came for the dogs, stayed for the kingdom. The game has a lot to do. Almost everything can be upgraded. Fighting is pretty fun. There’s a few currencies. It’s very overwhelming at first. After a few days of playing, I was kind of getting used to it. All the different things to do are very convoluted. There are free goodies hidden in various places. I think all currencies are attainable in the game. Of course, the game tries hard to get the player to buy all sorts of stuff. I bought a second building add-on so I could build 2 things at once. It was supposed to cost $1 but they charged me $2. Not a big deal but it’s NOT what I paid for. It was labeled “survival challenge” which is definitely something different. They have “unions” you can join. It’s pretty cool. You can ask for help to complete tasks like building and fighting. After a while the help for building doesn’t really help because building takes too long. There are also union battles and misc events. The biggest problem with these types of games is after a while, upgrading starts to take forever. There are in game items to speed things up but it shouldn’t take 24 hours in real time to upgrade a building. It just gets too ridiculous.

title: AI Generated Fake Positive Reviews
body: Search for “Most Critical” reviews to get a taste of why downloading this app is a huge mistake. First, to even open the app you have to give it full tracking permissions. Huge red flag but, most real human reviews will agree this game is a bait and switch. Whatever it’s been advertised as being, this isn’t it. The positive reviews are fake and developers use A.I. to respond to their reviews. If you read the reviews it is laughable how their AI mistakes a fake positive review as a negative review and it apologises for the experience the “user” describes as a positive experience. It all just smacks of a sophisticated phishing scheme. RUN. Just run from apps like this.
